name: Should I hire a general contractor or manage subcontractors myself for a foreclosure rehab?

mainEntity.name: Should I hire a general contractor or manage subcontractors myself for a foreclosure rehab?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hiring a general contractor provides a single point of accountability for complex multi-trade projects, whereas hiring separate subcontractors requires you to manage scheduling, quality control, and sequencing yourself. In a foreclosed home, work must happen in a strict order: framing and rough-in repairs must be inspected and finalized before hanging drywall, setting tile, or installing trim. If you manage trades independently, an error by one trade can cause scheduling delays and finger-pointing across the board. A hands-on contractor who performs the core finish trades directly while managing specialized mechanical sub-trades ensures consistent jobsite oversight and fewer coordination bottlenecks.
acceptedAnswer.description: A general contractor coordinates the required order of trades and manages on-site quality, preventing scheduling bottlenecks and delays common when managing trades solo.
